advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound the `remote_exists` probe inside `pending_init_remote_unreachable` (e.g. call `remote_exists(..., run_git_fn=_probe_git)` before the `ls-remote` classification) so every local `remote get-url` uses the bounded seam.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/_probe_git docstring at init.py:66-67: "bounded by :func:`_git`, where plain ``run_git`` carries no timeout at all"
advisory.finding: `pending_init_remote_unreachable` still passes `run_git_fn=run_git` to `remote_branch_unreachable`, which calls `remote_exists`, so its local `remote get-url` probe has no timeout. This contradicts the commit's claim that the local `remote get-url` probes now go through the bounded seam. During auto-init, `_choose_init_path` runs this predicate right after `pending_init_attaches_to_existing`, so a git that stalls at that point can still hang auto-init.
scenarios: Auto-init in a repo whose git starts stalling after the attach check: the unreachable-remote check's `remote get-url` blocks with no bound instead of raising GitTimedOut.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `pending_init_remote_unreachable`, check `has_ref` and `_init_probe.remote_exists(repo, remote_name, run_git_fn=_probe_git)` first, then call `probe_remote_branch(..., run_git_fn=run_git)` for the network probe. Passing `_probe_git` straight into `remote_branch_unreachable` would not work: it would also route `ls-remote` through `_probe_git`, which drops its `timeout=` kwarg.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Before resuming, make `_finish_bootstrap` check that the tracker is on the configured tickets branch (symbolic-ref) and that the index is empty when HEAD is unborn, and clear the index or redo the fallback otherwise.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/init.py:304-312: root commit `commit --allow-empty -q --no-verify` commits whatever is staged
src/rebar/_commands/init.py:551: `_commit_precommit` checks `tickets:.pre-commit-config.yaml`, which is absent on a detached host HEAD, so it commits there
advisory.finding: The resume guard in `_finish_bootstrap` treats 'HEAD unborn' as 'ready for the root commit'. On the git<2.40 fallback path that is not enough. If `rm -rf . --quiet` times out after `checkout --orphan`, HEAD is unborn but the index still holds the host repo's files, so the next init's resumed `commit --allow-empty` commits the host tree as the tickets branch's root. If `checkout --orphan` itself times out, HEAD is detached at a host commit, so the guard skips the root commit and `_commit_precommit` commits onto that detached host history.
scenarios: git < 2.40, a stalled filesystem: `rm -rf .` times out, the marker stays, and the next `rebar init` resumes and commits every host file into the tickets root commit.
git < 2.40: `checkout --orphan` times out, and resume commits .pre-commit-config.yaml onto a detached HEAD at the host commit, with no tickets branch.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Skip leading `-c <k=v>` pairs when deriving the GitTimedOut operation name in `_git`.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/init.py:170: `f"Error: {exc} during rebar init; nothing after it ran. "`
advisory.finding: `_git` builds the GitTimedOut operation name from `args[:2]`. For the `-c`-prefixed rebase call this gives `-c rebase.autostash=true`, so the user sees 'Error: git -c rebase.autostash=true timed out during rebar init', which does not name the command that stalled.
scenarios: A stalled `rebase --continue` during re-init reports a `-c` config option instead of `rebase --continue`.
advisory.suggested_fix: Strip leading `-c <k=v>` pairs before taking the first two args: `rest = list(args)` then `while rest[:1] == ['-c']: rest = rest[2:]`, and use `' '.join(rest[:2])`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests that start the stall after the `rev-parse --verify <remote>/<branch>` call and assert that the first stalled call is `remote get-url`, once through init_core (line 437) and once through pending_init_attaches_to_existing / _create_tracker (line 623).
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/init.py:407: `_init_probe.require_s3_helper_if_s3_remote(repo, remote_name, run_git_fn=_probe_git)` — the only probe the test reaches first
test: `stalled = _stall(monkeypatch)` then `assert stalled and stalled[0][:2] == ("remote", "get-url")` — the assertion only looks at stalled[0], which comes from line 407

test_auto_init_reports_a_timeout_instead_of_creating_a_store calls `_stall(monkeypatch)` with no `after`, so pending_init_attaches_to_existing raises at `_git_ok(repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", branch)` (init.py:619) before it reaches remote_exists
The stub replaces only `run_git_write`, so a reverted `run_git_fn=run_git` would call real git, never record a stalled call, and still pass
advisory.finding: test_the_remote_probes_go_through_the_bounded_seam only checks the first `remote get-url` probe, from require_s3_helper_if_s3_remote at line 407. The diff also switches `_init_probe.remote_exists(..., run_git_fn=_probe_git)` at init.py:437 (_mount_or_create_branch) and init.py:623 (pending_init_attaches_to_existing) from unbounded run_git to _probe_git. Changing either back to run_git would leave every test green. The auto-init test stalls from the very first call, so its first timeout is the `rev-parse --verify` at line 619 and line 623 is never reached.
scenarios: A repo with `origin` configured and no local or remote-tracking tickets branch, where git stalls from the `rev-parse --verify origin/tickets` call onward. If line 437 or 623 goes back to run_git, the `remote get-url` probe hangs unbounded, as described in the bug, and no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reuse `_stall(monkeypatch, after=lambda a: a[:2] == ("rev-parse", "--verify") and "/" in a[-1])` in a repo with `git remote add origin <path>`. Call `init.pending_init_attaches_to_existing(str(repo))` inside `pytest.raises(GitTimedOut)` and assert `stalled[0][:2] == ("remote", "get-url")`. Do the same through init_core, with the pin skipped and require_s3_helper stubbed, to cover line 437.
